title: Knowledge check: Static, Media, and Deployment Failures

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed for “Static, Media, and Deployment Failures”?
options: A complete substitute for server-side validation
A guarantee that every database write succeeds atomically
A feature that is always enabled without configuration
questions.explanation: The supplied Django curriculum lists “Static file discovery” under lesson 260, “Static, Media, and Deployment Failures”. The lesson connects this item to the practical Django workflow for troubleshooting and legacy compatibility.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports reliable work on “Static, Media, and Deployment Failures”?
options: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
Assume the browser is trusted and skip server-side checks.
Copy a production secret into the source file so every environment matches.
Publish an example before checking framework/version compatibility.
questions.answer_key: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproducible examples, server-side validation where relevant, and explicit positive/negative checks help distinguish expected behavior from assumptions. Version, environment, and boundary cases should be documented.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most appropriate when applying “Static, Media, and Deployment Failures” in a real application?
options: Delete migration history whenever there is a conflict.
Ignore reproducibility and rely on a clean local machine.
Keep a small regression test for the observed fault and verify the fix.
questions.answer_key: Keep a small regression test for the observed fault and verify the fix.
questions.explanation: The lesson is part of Troubleshooting and Legacy Compatibility. Select the approach that supports correctness, safe handling of failures, and verifiable behavior; see the linked official documentation for version-specific details.

notes: Answer keys and explanations remain in the server-side course repository. The existing CodeLeaf GET handler strips answers until grading; this course does not expose solutions in public lesson content.
